claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy can form a protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure to molten aluminum.
The protective oxide scale formed on the tungsten-based RHEA reduces erosion by molten aluminum.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation processing produces coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The SCCP-processed tungsten RHEA combines high strength and ductility at elevated temperatures.
The proposed components will operate in long-term contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote a stable microstructure during the proposed service exposure.
Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate formation of a protective oxide scale on the alloy surface.
A CrTaO4-based protective oxide scale can form on an RHEA during high-temperature oxidation.
The SCCP-structured tungsten RHEA maintains structural integrity at high temperature.
The oxide layer acts as a chemical barrier against attack by liquid aluminum.
Components made from the proposed tungsten-based RHEA will have significantly lower material loss than conventional components.
Components made from the proposed tungsten-based RHEA will have a longer service life than conventional components.
The predicted improvement results from continuous self-protecting oxide-layer formation.
Conventional lower-melting-point or non-optimized alloys rapidly corrode in high-temperature molten aluminum.
Successful protection depends on reliable formation and long-term adhesion of the oxide scale under thermal cycling and aluminum-bath impurities.
The long-term stability of the proposed protective oxide in an actual hot-dip aluminum plating environment has not been experimentally verified.
